properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-30, continuing the governance thread: *"what if instead of creating new tools for governance and management, it was instead built into each tool... it is kind of like our idea to compose skills from a set of classes. for instance, if a tool that writes to the graph is used, maybe it has a governance edge, 'push design changes to GitHub repo using git worktree branch, never to main directly'... there could be other governance/management type fields that get added based on the type of node/edge it is."*

⭐ THREE NODES ALREADY HOLD PARTS OF THIS, AND ONE OF THEM IS HIS OWN, STILL UNACCEPTED.

· `req:the-reminder-rides-the-response` — **status `proposed` since 2026-08-19**, his words: *"how come we can't attach a parameter to each skill request that returns something to the user."* It states the principle in general form — *a discipline that must survive context distance belongs on the wire, not in a file* — and already records that `loop_hint` / `with_loop_hint` in service.rs is the proven carrier. It also records a real narrowing: **his proposal was an INPUT parameter, what is owed is an OUTPUT**, because an input has a chicken-and-egg. ELEVEN DAYS LATER IT IS STILL WAITING ON HIM, while today's remark restates it.
· `req:a-discipline-is-delivered-at-the-tool-not-in-a-catalogue` — ACCEPTED. Task-skills are reached for at a boundary; discipline-skills apply mid-flow, and *"a catalogue structurally cannot serve the second"* because it is read once.
· `dec:idea-search-first-fires-without-being-remembered` — the same shape for one specific discipline: search-before-you-add is written into five skills and still depends on somebody loading one.
· `fact:a-skill-is-loaded-only-when-something-already-in-hand-demands-it` — the measured ROOT CAUSE: *"No reflow2 tool makes any reflow2 skill a precondition of itself."* One skill in a long session loaded because a NON-reflow2 tool (`Artifact`) declared it a precondition. **The mechanism he is describing is already proven to work — by somebody else's tool.**

═══ WHAT IS GENUINELY NEW TODAY, AND WHY THIS IS A SEPARATE NODE ═══

(1) **KEYED ON THE TYPE, NOT PLACED PER TOOL.** The obligation attaches to the KIND of thing acted on — a graph write, a node of this type, an edge of that type — so a NEW tool that writes inherits the write-obligations without anyone remembering to wire it. `loop_hint` is computed and hand-placed per call site; this is compositional, and it is the half his skill-classes analogy (`composes: [STANDING, WRITES, MINTS, MEASURES]`, which exists on skills and not on tools) actually points at.

(2) **THE USER SUPPLIES THE OBLIGATION.** Every instance above is a discipline REFLOW2 knows about ITSELF. His example happens to be one reflow2 holds (`rule:nothing-lands-on-main-directly`), but his brother's employer has GitLab push rules reflow2 has never heard of. `governance-proposal` CAPTURES a user's rule; nothing DELIVERS it at the moment of the act. Capture without delivery is the gap.

Neither is in the three nodes above, which is why this is recorded beside them rather than merged into one.

═══ OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN ═══
(a) EXTEND `loop_hint` INTO A TYPED OBLIGATION CHANNEL — same proven carrier, content composed from the types touched plus any user rules that match. Smallest step from what exists.
(b) TOOLS DECLARE A REQUIRED SKILL, the way `Artifact` requires `artifact-design`. Attacks the measured root cause directly and is the one shape already observed to work on this agent.
(c) BOTH — (b) where a discipline has a procedure behind it, (a) for one-line obligations needing no skill.
(d) NOTHING NEW: accept `req:the-reminder-rides-the-response` first and see what its delivery naturally covers, since today's idea may be a special case rather than a separate feature.

⚠️ THE FAILURE MODE TO DESIGN AGAINST, and it already retired a detector here: an obligation on every write becomes noise, and noise is how a real warning stops being read. `unexpected_coupling` was retired for firing on correct architecture; `loop_hint` answered the same pressure with a fire-on-change throttle. Anything built here needs a rationing story before it needs features.

NOT ESTABLISHED: whether a user-supplied obligation is new vocabulary or an existing DesignRule with a trigger; and whether anything READS it, which `req:a-vocabulary-distinction-proves-it-is-read` demands before it is added.
properties.name: OPEN — governance as a property of each TOOL rather than a new set of nodes: keyed on the node/edge type acted on, and suppliable by the USER
properties.rationale: Captured under the brainstorm skill; the current increment stays the priority. Recorded beside `req:the-reminder-rides-the-response` rather than merged into it because two parts of today's remark — keying the obligation on the node/edge TYPE so new tools inherit it, and letting the USER supply the rule — are absent from that requirement, which concerns reflow2 delivering disciplines it already knows about itself. The overlap is named in the text so a later reader finds one line of reasoning rather than three lookalike ideas.
